budgets._doc: Injection budgets in BYTES per point (EVOL-043). One reader measures the REAL producer at its worst case: python3 scripts/gate.py budget. Raising a key needs its record in the changelog. prompt_submit ≥ snapshot + the reload wrapper + the stale warning (the worst case forces both).

agents._doc: EVOL-049: the two model FAMILIES as harness aliases (never pinned ids; SETUP Q34) — writers and critics on different families by construction (gate.py agents refuses equal aliases). The class policy, the roster and the per-spawn resolution live in .claude/rules/agents.md.

coherence._doc: Coherence gates (EVOL-044). certifying_artefacts: the verdict artefacts gate.py currency judges (terminal status/verdict must carry certifies: from gate.py certify). Empty list = a ratified opt-out.

surface._doc: Per-PR surface ceiling (EVOL-045). The reviewable unit is bounded per pull request: python3 scripts/gate.py surface measures files + lines of the diff vs the one diff base (gate.py diff-base) with no exclusion list; over a ceiling blocks the push unless a commit trailer `Surface-Escape: <term>` names one of `escapes` (closed vocabulary — extending it needs a decision record). EVOL-047: runtime_surface is the POSITIVE list every deploying / release workflow asks before running its machinery (python3 scripts/gate.py runtime-surface --changed); always_deploy = hard exclusions that fire it regardless, each with its reason (workflow definitions; inputs a deployment-time gate reads); declared_reads = paths a deploying job reads outside the surface, each with its reason (parity exemptions, glob allowed). deploying_workflows = the deploying / release-cutting workflow files the parity gate reads (resolved at SETUP from Q21; add the project's own deploy workflows). gate.py runtime-surface (a member of the gate profile, CI) holds the list to what the jobs and their scripts really read. The branch rule is untouched: every change ships via branch and pull request. Ceilings asked at SETUP Q31.

always_deploy.reason: workflow definitions execute in CI/CD — a change here must run (the CI platform's own files, resolved at SETUP from Q21)
input of the deployment-time gates (surface, profile)
the framework version and delivery mode the deployment-time gates read (gate.py profile) — a mode change always runs the machinery

planning._doc: One planning stage (EVOL-048): a write to a governed path on a branch class with no framework planning phase needs an approved plan (python3 scripts/gate.py plan --path P; the PreToolUse hook check-plan-approval.sh asks it). governed_paths minus the documentation class (config → documentation, EVOL-051), except gate_inputs (documents a gate reads — governed like code). exempt_classes: the classes whose plan a framework phase owns; every other class is gated (fail-closed). plan_artefact: the branch's own plan artefact ({ID} = feature id) counts when its frontmatter status is approved. The approval marker is written only by the harness's plan approval (PostToolUse ExitPlanMode → gate.py plan --record); a marker approved on a base branch is adopted once, within adoption_window_minutes; an approval older than approval_ttl_hours no longer counts. The behavioural contracts under .claude/ and the workflow files are gate inputs — never documentation. Project: feature, increment, train, sub-increment and epic branches are planned by CODESIGN / BLUEPRINT / IMPLEMENT --plan; a fix, a chore, a docs or a breaking branch is gated. governed_paths is resolved at SETUP as the runtime surface (Q33) plus the governance paths; the plan artefact is never a gate input; increment_plan.md is one (it decides whether a branch is a protected train).

documentation._doc: The ONE definition of a documentation path (EVOL-051): root-anchored globs in `paths`, minus `exclusions` (code whatever the extension). Read by python3 scripts/gate.py documentation — the push-gate preflight's review-lane skip, the planning gate's exemption (planning.docs_exempt is retired) and the seal's classification. A workflow or a behavioural contract (.claude/{instructions,skills,commands,hooks}) is never documentation.

verification._doc: One full verification loop per change (EVOL-051): `gates` is the path-to-gate map (what each full-loop gate READS, and the command that runs it — a command shared by two gates, e.g. tests and coverage, is executed once and feeds both); `seal` is where python3 scripts/gate.py seal records a green loop per branch (untracked, .claude/state/) — the push refuses a tree the seal does not cover (gate.py seal --check, a profile member); a changed path no gate reads and no documentation class covers owes the full loop (fail closed: declare its reader). `digest_artefacts` are the planning artefacts gate.py digests judges under docs/spec/{ID}/ (fingerprint = the snapshot's constitution_hash[:8]; every bound rule named).

traceability._doc: Test-case traceability (EVOL-053): the ONE machine-readable home of the case → test link (`home`: kind pytest-marker | title-tag, or a custom `pattern` with a named group `id`), the case grammar (`id_pattern`; a link is FEATURE/CASE — the plan folder and the id its test_plan.md declares), the plans, the test roots and the shrink-only baseline (docs/project_log/traceability_baseline.json — `gate.py traceability --baseline --init` records the debt once, `--refresh` shrinks it, never adds). python3 scripts/gate.py traceability is a light member of the gate profile (static round, push, CI): every declared case has a linking test or sits in the baseline; a link naming no declared case is red; QA consumes `--json` instead of re-deriving the linkage.

scm._doc: Server-side branch protection (EVOL-054): the SCM host (`platform`: GitHub | GitLab | Bitbucket | Azure DevOps | Other — SETUP Q21.2), the protected branches, the checks the server must require before a merge and the approvals the project decided (Q21.2, 0 for a single author — never invented). python3 scripts/gate.py scm-protection is a member of the gate profile at the ci control point: with a read-only token in the CI environment (GITHUB_TOKEN / GH_TOKEN, GITLAB_TOKEN, BITBUCKET_TOKEN as user:app_password, AZURE_DEVOPS_TOKEN) it asks the platform's API per protected branch and is RED on a missing setting; without a token, for `Other`, at push or at the static round it is n/a with the checklist. The runbook with the exact settings is docs/scm/protection.md (materialised per platform). protected_branches names the default branch — the same name rules/branching.md carries as default_base_branch; a project on master or develop edits both.
